analysis.title: Hayward Holdings (HAYW): 3Q26 results solid; FY26 guidance raised as share gains continue and early-buy trends encouraging; Neutral
key_insights: HAYW 3Q26 revenue was $260mn, up 6% yoy, above GSe/FactSet consensus of $253mn/$252mn. Net pricing rose 5%, volumes rose 1%, and FX was about flat.

North America revenue rose 9% yoy to $226mn (net price +7%, volume +2%). U.S. sales rose 10% and Canada fell 9%. Europe and ROW revenue fell 6% to $34mn, about -1% excluding China shipments that shifted from 3Q into 4Q.
Gross margin rose 10bps yoy to 47.9% and adj. EBITDA margin expanded 60bps to 24.8%. Adj. EBITDA rose 9% to $65mn versus GSe/consensus of $56mn/$59mn.
3Q26 adj. EPS was $0.18, up 29% yoy, versus GSe/consensus of $0.13/$0.15.

FY26 sales growth guidance was raised to +5%-6% yoy from ~5%, implying revenue of ~$1.18bn-$1.19bn versus GSe/consensus of $1.18bn. Adj. EPS guidance was raised to $0.86-$0.88 from $0.84-$0.87, with the midpoint above GSe/consensus of $0.85/$0.86.

The guidance implies 4Q sales growth of roughly 0%-3% yoy and adj. EPS of $0.28-$0.30. It assumes low-to-mid-single-digit positive pricing, volume as the main swing factor, and no repeat of last year's strong late-season orders. More discounted early-buy sales also make 4Q price/mix less favorable.
Management still expects FY26 gross margin of ~48%, roughly in line with 2025's record level, despite slightly above mid-single-digit inflation.

Share gains are described as broad-based and durable across regions, product categories and dealer types, with strength in sanitization, automation and controls, and LED lighting. U.S. channel partners report strong sell-through despite weak new pool construction.

2027 early-buy orders in North America are tracking above the prior year. Management expects low-single-digit volume growth once the program closes and mid-single-digit gross pricing, modestly lower than last year. Early-buy is ~30% and no more than one-third of annual purchases.

Management expects dealer conversions to support above-market volume growth even in a flat 2027 industry. It is not assuming any improvement in new construction. COVID-era pool equipment should begin entering the typical 7-10 year replacement window over the next year-plus, a potential aftermarket tailwind.

HAYW ended 3Q26 with $475mn of cash and $900mn of total liquidity, with net leverage at 1.5x. It repurchased 3.4mn shares (~1.5% of shares outstanding) for $51mn ($15.18/sh) in the quarter and 7.8mn shares for $115mn ($14.76) YTD. $331mn remains under the $450mn authorization.
YTD FCF fell to $196mn from $262mn, largely on higher working capital from late-quarter shipments and inventory built for the larger early-buy program.

GS raised its 12-month price target to $16 from $14, based on 12x EV/EBITDA (from 11x) applied to Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA, citing a better setup into 2027 and a model roll-forward. Rating stays Neutral. Implied upside is 22.8% from $13.03.
GS raised estimates: 2026E/2027E/2028E adj. EBITDA to $318mn/$336mn/$350mn from $316mn/$330mn/$349mn. Adj. EPS goes to $0.87/$0.97/$1.03 from $0.85/$0.91/$0.98.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised the target to $16 from $14 on a 12x EV/EBITDA multiple (11x prior) and a roll-forward, citing a better 2027 setup. The rating stays Neutral.

tension_points.bull_case: Early-buy orders are tracking above the prior year, with low-single-digit volume growth expected once the program closes. Share gains are broad-based, channel inventories are healthy, and COVID-era pool equipment is entering its replacement window.
tension_points.bear_case: New pool construction remains weak and management is not assuming an improvement. 4Q guidance does not assume a repeat of last year's strong late-season orders, and volume is the main swing factor.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Early-buy volumes falling below the prior year, or a shorter or longer than expected channel inventory correction.

theme_stances.key_argument: Continued share gains, healthy channel inventories and positive early-buy volumes are a supportive initial read on 2027, though new construction is not assumed to improve.
theme_stances.evidence: continued share gains, healthy channel inventories, and positive early-buy volumes
